new_reference.definition: [^v1-c1-rees]: Martin Rees, *Just Six Numbers* (1999), on six selected quantities shaping cosmic structure, rather than an exhaustive list of fundamental constants. For $Q$, see Max Tegmark and Martin J. Rees, [“Why Is the Cosmic Microwave Background Fluctuation Level $10^{-5}$?”](https://arxiv.org/html/astro-ph/9709058v2), *Astrophysical Journal* 499 (1998): 526–532, §§1, 3–5. Their star-formation and orbital-disruption arguments depend on model assumptions; §5 shows why varying parameters together changes anthropic bounds.

new_reference.qualifications: Q is order-of-magnitude shorthand for primordial fluctuation strength, not all fluctuations at every scale. Viability bounds depend on assumptions; no universal exact threshold, probability of our universe, or proof of design is claimed.
